source_caption:
🎬 Paycheck (2003)

Paycheck follows Michael Jennings, a brilliant computer engineer who earns enormous amounts of money by working on highly classified projects and allowing his memory to be erased after each assignment. When he accepts a mysterious three-year job for a powerful technology company, he expects to receive a massive paycheck upon completion. However, after his memory is erased, Michael discovers that he has voluntarily surrendered his fortune in exchange for an envelope containing seemingly worthless everyday objects. Confused and pursued by dangerous government agents, he soon realizes that the objects are clues left by his past self to help him survive a deadly conspiracy. With the help of scientist Rachel Porter, Michael races against time to uncover the truth about his missing memories and a revolutionary invention capable of predicting the future. Starring Ben Affleck and Uma Thurman, Paycheck combines thrilling action, suspense, science fiction, and unexpected twists while exploring memory, destiny, free will, and the consequences of knowing what lies ahead.

🎭 Genre: Action • Mystery • Sci-Fi • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 6.3/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 59m • PG-13

🎥 Director: John Woo

✍️ Writer: Dean Georgaris, based on a story by Philip K. Dick

source_details.synopsis: Paycheck is a 2003 American science fiction action film directed and produced by John Woo. It was written by Dean Georgaris, based on the 1953 short story by Philip K. Dick. Starring Ben Affleck, Aaron Eckhart, and Uma Thurman, with Paul Giamatti, Colm Feore, Joe Morton, and Michael C. Hall in supporting roles, the film follows a reverse engineer who finds himself hunted by both the FBI and a tech CEO after his memory is erased. Paycheck was released on December 25, 2003, by Paramount Pictures in North America and DreamWorks Pictures internationally to negative reviews from critics and grossed $117.2 million against a $60 million budget.
